steps.text: 7:11 A.M. \ Overcast
Rhodes Island County Hillock Branch Office

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Morning, everyone! The weather's not bad at all today, wouldn't you say, Uncle Oliver?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Oh, it's you. I was just asking, who else could it be knocking at the crack of dawn? But it's a gloomy day today no matter where you look. What's to appreciate?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Any time it's not raining is good weather. That's what you get in County Hillock. For that matter, how do you know the day's not going to turn clear skies?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Fine, you've got me there. Shredder, you stop dilly-dallying. We haven't got anyone dropping in, it's just Janie, daily ditcher.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You're one to talk. Shredder, you come over here with us.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I brought you a yuccoffee pie today, and some shortbread. Da sent me some tea last week, so I've brought that too. Uncle Oliver, is there any evaporated milk left?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Leftovers started molding ages ago. That bloody man—never remembers to go buy any.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Isn't it your turn on the shopping? Or am I hallucinating, somehow?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Fred! Will! We need your thoughts too!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Alright, alright, it's not worth crying over this little spilled milk. Look, what's this? Fresh new evaporated, and some cheese too. Picked them up along the way from the morning market. Here, you can have them.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Hee-hee, I've wanted to try making milk tea for forever now. I think you'll like it at least, Uncle Oliver.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Ah, still no one more considerate than you, Janie. Will, you'd better learn well. At least don't start acting like that man next to you with Shredder for a codename.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: This shortbread tastes delicious... ooh, right, Miss Willow, isn't your senior officer going to get on your case for running here every day to bring us breakfast?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: The Victorian Army's rules are a fair deal strict, if I recall.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Ah... you don't need to worry about that. I'm a guard of honor, I'm only good for big events or recruitment drives. They don't have much use to put me to—the Sergeant Major wouldn't even think about me most of the time.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Besides, it's not like I don't do anything proper.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Every morning when I get up, the first thing I do is pull this banner off its support.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: While I wait for the flour to ferment and the coffee to brew, I'll straighten out the creases bit by bit.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Once the shortbread's done, that means I have to wash the flour off me. It takes time for my hair to dry naturally, and that's the perfect time to care for the flagpole, and let it shine like brand new.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Uncle Oliver, don't rush to pick up your tea yet—it's still too hot.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: For a complete morning, everything needs to glow gorgeous, no exceptions. Only then can I bring joy to you all—that's my life's creed.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: What's the pie like today, Shredder? Want any more?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Perfect... Just like every day before.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Really? Let me try some too... seems I put a little too much sugar in. I'll make sure to watch out for that tomorrow.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: Well, I'm not going to tell you off for being lazy like they do now, Miss Willow.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: —Janie. That's what everyone calls me.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: Alright, er... Miss Jane. My honest fear's that they'll want me spending every morning as amply as you do.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: No need for that. I'm not like any of you, there's only so much I can do for the people here. Hm... I think the tea's about the right temperature now. Just make sure to stir it a little before you drink—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Yagh!

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: You sent the ball flyin' again, Craig!

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: I'll go get it.

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: Oh, poo... it went in the building.

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: If you actually hit any of the grown-ups, then, then you're in for it! Last time, didn't Carol get...

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: *Huff*, *huff*... Someone's come out, let's run!

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Whose ball is this?

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Is it yours?

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: Craig... Craig, come on, run! Forget the ball...

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: No... that ball's left by my da...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If you're too shy about it, I won't hand it back. Come on, hold your hand out.

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Are... Are you gonna beat me?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Why would I beat you, now?

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Your clothes got dirty.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Eh, that's just me being careless. It's no matter.

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: All the other grown-ups like you, they don't care if it wasn't me who got them dirty.

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: They always beat us. But not with their hands, they kick us instead. And they shout all loud, to scare us off.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: That means they're definitely not your friends.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Do you live around here? I think I've spotted you before. Doesn't your ma sell apples at the crack of every dawn, down the alley in District Seventeen nearby?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Your family's apples are scrumptious. Not too crisp, but still very, very sweet. Perfect for making apple butter and spreading onto bread.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: How about this? I'll put the ball on the windowsill here, and you come pick it up, okay?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Hold on, slow down, I've got tea on my hands, it's gotten your hair all wet. Let me wipe that for you.

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I'm Janie. What's your name?

steps.name: Anxious Child A
steps.text: Craig! It's your ma lookin' for you. Quick, you've gotta go!

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Got into a commotion outside?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Children playing ball.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Those bunch of rotters, all higgledy-piggledly in the street first thing in the morning. I bet it was them who broke that last windowpane, too.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Haha... children, you know? I broke the man next door's flowerpots when I was young, and my da really gave me a talking-to for that.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: You laid hands on that boy.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Just now? Yeah, if I didn't wipe his hair clean, it'd be sticky all day.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: His father passed away, half a year ago. Poor bloke, caught Oripathy.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: There's a lot—'cause of that—won't dare touch him.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Workers, fairly strapped for cash. That Oriron byproduct processing plant has a partnership, with Aneca. But they don't give the full amount of prophylactics.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: It's normal for you—to hesitate. In their neighborhood, it's about one in five houses, turning out to have Oripathy patients.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: They care for another, in a sense. If those soldiers weren't here...

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Shredder! You've lost track.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's alright... you're just stating the facts. I've heard how... my coworkers treat the Oripathy-sick... no, not just the sick, they've got the wrong idea about all of the residents.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I... I don't think the same way. We're all Victorians, aren't we? Their days might be hard on them, I—I understand full well. But I hope for them to live a little happier too.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: What do you think... Should I have been even better to that child?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: ...Don't force yourself.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: What's the long faces for? I'll bring the playing cards out. Wasn't it you who suggested a spot of tea with cards, Miss Jane?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Yes. Will's right, the sun's poking out for once in a while. Let's not waste the good weather.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Take a seat, everyone. I'll pour you all some more tea; there's still plenty left in the pot.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: Is that me who's won again?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: It's too early to be full of yourself. You're on shift tonight.

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: What? How's it me again?!

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Not clicking? That was our stakes! Whoever won at cards is on broom duty, file sorting, buying us all afternoon tea...

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: Can I get a redeal?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Uncle Oliver, your jokes are putting Will in tears again.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Isn't that the fun of a game of cards? Ha-ha-ha-ha!
One small tip—next time you try second dealing, remember to watch behind you.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: What—?! Who's talking?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And on a side note, the tea's an excellent brew.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: H—Hello! Who might you be?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (She came in suddenly, and none of us noticed her...)

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: They call me Outcast, my young Vouivran beauty.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'm sorry I tasted your tea without asking. Seeing as I rushed all the way over here, I hope you won't mind too much.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: F... Feel—feel free. If you haven't eaten breakfast yet, would you like to try some pie I baked? It might be a little sweet...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'd love to. Everybody who knows me knows I love sweets—especially the Victorian kind. You got it baked like this to fancy, adorable perfection.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Haha... Thank you for the encouragement, Lady Outcast.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: —Outcast. Nobody calls me a Lady, really. I'm more of that 'Lass' type.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: I—I know who you are! I remember now... Will! C-Clean the table up, quick—

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: I thought you'd be here two days later... Last message, you said you'd just passed the border.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Couldn't help it, I haven't been to Victoria in a decade. Some parts are a bit more crowded, but just like me, the years are starting to show in a few places.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: If I hadn't hitched a ride the wrong way in County Peninsula, we would've met last night.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: *cough* Ahem, your understanding, please. County Hillock's not the biggest spot on the map, and we rarely get elite operators at our branch office here.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Last time I was out near Minos on field work, I met Stormeye—that was two years ago, already.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Elite operator? Just the name sounds like a force to be reckoned with.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: —Rhodes Island gives different work to different people, that's all. Besides, I'm pretty much just a civil servant now. I only came to County Hillock to fetch some data.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: You're too modest.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: On the topic of data, did you want to see our finance forms first, or the ledger for our inventory in/out and stock this half... (Hints to Will)

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Hold your beasties.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: We're not THAT pressed for time. No need to hurl a starving girl like me straight into work. It's only fair to let me steal a breather here and there, right?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Haha... I can sympathize greatly.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Hope I haven't disrupted your little R&R here.

a.text: Outcast casually picks up a card. Thin, no more than paper, it spins three times and a half at her fingertips, then is gone in a swish.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Wow! Where'd that card just go?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Right here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's back! What kind of marvelous spatial Arts is this?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Just a little sleight of hand. I've got this gloomy-looking friend who taught me. Whenever I want you concentrating on my fingertips, this method works wonders.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: All a little more relaxed now? Please, sit down, Oliver, and Shredder, Will, plus you there, kiddo, standing in the corner—you must be Fred.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Put that folder down, and enjoy a little break with us. A chance like this doesn't come every day.

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: A... Are you sure this is okay?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Or would you like to see a magic trick where in ten minutes, this haggard stranger from out of town dies of boredom?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: *cough* Let's sit.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Please, continue.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: As for me, I still want a proper taste of this fine black tea with evaporated milk, and that sweet, scrumptious pie.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Ah, there's more shortbread left here, if you still feel hungry, that is...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Ahh, now this dessert hit the spot. My stomach hasn't been this happy in a while. My tongue was beginning to really miss flavor.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Now, you, cute little miss—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I—I'm Jane, Jane Willow.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That's a lovely name. I'm gonna guess you're old enough to drink?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I've long since been of age, La... Lass.. Outcast. I'm serving, after all.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Oh? That gray Victorian military uniform sure falls flat under your shimmering blonde hair. Oliver, count yourself lucky. No matter how dull and cloudy it gets, you've always got your sunshine indoors.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Haha... true, true. Little Janie's brought us a mound of happy days.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Listen to you, Uncle Oliver. You're the ones all kindly letting me in while I've snuck off from the barracks.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I was actually a tiny bit surprised, seeing you get along as well as you do—

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Jane, if all Victorian soldiers were as lovable as you, we'd lose at least half of those awful rumors making their way across our world.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Thank you, if I haven't misunderstood. I assume those are compliments...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Even on my way here, I saw some not-so-pretty sights. But anyhow, that's not gonna dampen the joy of meeting all of you here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I'm very glad... I could meet you too!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Well, then, a toast to our encounter?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I came here in kind of a hurry, so I could only bring some regular old gin, with way too much lemon because that's how I like it. You folks might find it too sour—

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: We don't really drink... on work hours.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: You killjoy!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Alright, that's on me for being sloppy. As a Rhodes Island Operator, I can't be an exception. Let's just have some tea.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: So—who's dealing next?

steps.name: Operator Will
steps.text: M—Me.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Need a little blessing from a Sankta?
